paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this passage. The queen of Sheba heard a report and didn't just nod along. She went and checked it out for herself. Then she said, "I did not believe the reports until I came and saw with my own eyes." (2 Chronicles 9:6) Hearing about something good is nice, but seeing it up close is a whole different batch.

Look at where her praise lands. She calls Solomon's servants blessed for hearing his wisdom, but then she says, "Blessed be the LORD your God, who has delighted in you to set you on His throne…" (2 Chronicles 9:8) She saw a great king, and she traced it all back to the LORD. She also says that God made him king "to carry out justice and righteousness." (2 Chronicles 9:8) Wisdom and power were given to Solomon so that he could serve others well.

So here's the lesson for you, baker. Don't settle for secondhand. Come and taste the Word for yourself, because it will be even better than what you were told. And when somebody's life or work impresses you, let it point you to the God who gave it, because that's exactly what she did.
